newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Feb. 12.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Feb. 12.

text.p: One major Mexican port was reported open Wednesday, and two crude ports reopened as weather conditions improved in the Gulf of Mexico, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in its 1000 local/1600 GMT daily report.
Crude ports Dos Bocas in Tabasco and Pajaritos in Veracruz reopened to exports at 0800 local/1400 GMT. The nation's largest crude port, Cayo Arcas, remained open amid the high wind velocities.
Frontera port in Yucatan state remained shut Wednesday amid winds of up to 40 km and waves as high as seven and eight feet.
The ministry advised ships to exercise caution in the Gulf of Tehuantepec because of strong winds and high waves.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.

Cold front leaving light rains and clouds over Baja California peninsula and Sonora and Sinaloa states. Winds between 10 and 20 knots (19 to 38 km/11 to 22 miles per hour) and waves three to five feet high. -- Gulf of Mexico:

Cold air mass settled along Tamaulipas and north Veracruz state. Mostly sunny skies along rest of shore, with winds 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 17 miles per hour) and waves three to five feet high.
Cloudy skies from southeast Gulf of Mexico and most of Caribbean, with moderate winds from east at 20 to 30 km.
